newsitem.title: UK: PowerGen dips despite top-end profits.
newsitem.headline: PowerGen dips despite top-end profits.

text.p: Shares in PowerGen Plc eased in pre-market trade on Thursday, as a slightly disappointing dividend and cautious comment on National Power Plc offset profits at the top end of forecasts, dealers said.
PowerGen shares were down 2p at 691-1/2 by 0718 GMT while National Power dropped 5-1/2p to 540.

Dealers said there was also caution over utility stocks ahead of next month's budget, expected to include a "windfall" tax on privatised companies designed to fund training and job creation programmes.
"The dividend was just a bit light and we are one month away from the budget," one said. "If you are buying PowerGen now, are you walking into a trap?"

Separately a report in the Financial Times, commenting on the market's reaction to the National Power figures, said there could be a similar disappointment in its fiscal 1998 figures after the company's warning of unexciting earnings growth.
PowerGen shares fell as much as 20p at one stage on Wednesday after lower-than-expected profits from National Power.
PowerGen posted a two percent rise in pre-tax profit rose to 575 million stg in the year ended March 30 and raised its dividend 20 percent to 25.2p per share.
Analyst expectactions had mostly ranged between 528 million stg and 592 million. The dividend was expected at between 25p and 26.3p.
Analyst Nigel Hawkins at Yamaichi said it was a good set of results that showed the company outperforming its larger rival.
Hawkins said the share price drop probably reflected nothing more than its strength in the run-up to the results -- it has risen some 18 percent since the start of April.
Hawkins highlighted 13 percent growth in PowerGen's earnings per share and contrasted its 20 percent dividend increase with the nine percent rise from National Power on Wednesday.
"It is a good set of results and certainly outshines National Power," Hawkins said.

Chairman Ed Wallis said the results demonstrated the success of the company's business in minimising the impact of the increasingly competitive UK electricity market. "This is a strategy that can support the long-term growth of the business," Wallis said. -- David Holmes, London Newsroom +44 171 542 4367
